modelAnswer.rationale: The 50 mm lever turns 60 N into about 3 N·m at the face, which is more than the direct shear and bending about the base (about 1.4 N·m at roughly H/2). The load enters at the centre through the fixed 31 mm bolt pattern, so the plate bends locally between the edge ribs. Plate stiffness D scales with t^3, so a is near -3; ribs of the same thickness scale more like t, so a ≈ -2.6. Wider W lengthens the unsupported span between the ribs, so b ≈ +1.2. Taller H raises the axis and the moment arm to the base, partly offset by deeper triangular ribs, so c ≈ +0.8.

leastSquaresOnHeldOut.note: fit to the held-out data itself: an upper bound, not a fair solver

reading: The model got the thickness and width trends right (t^-2.6, W^+1.2, larger than the measured +0.72) but the height trend wrong in sign (+0.8 vs the measured -0.37): taller plates with deeper ribs are stiffer at the axis here. It passes the bar, and the solver still decides.
